name: Vesicle Trafficking and Secretory Pathway
description: The secretory pathway in S. cerevisiae transports proteins from ER through Golgi to plasma membrane or extracellular space via COPII-coated vesicles (ER→Golgi), COPI vesicles (intra-Golgi), and secretory vesicles (Golgi→PM). Each vesicle budding and fusion event requires: cargo selection, coat assembly (Sar1, Sec23/24, Sec13/31 for COPII), vesicle scission, coat disassembly, tethering, SNARE pairing (v-SNARE + t-SNARE), and membrane fusion. Rab GTPases (Ypt1, Sec4) regulate vesicle identity and targeting. The pathway has extremely high AND gate requirements - all components must be present and properly assembled for successful transport. Nobel Prize to Schekman, Rothman, Südhof.
scientificAccuracy: Based on Nobel Prize-winning research on vesicle trafficking. All components validated in yeast genetic screens.
